_about: Site-selection settings shared by phase0/phase1/phase2/phase2b/phase3 (v2.0: Boolean screening + multi-criteria evaluation). Change values here, not in the Python code. Keys starting with '_' are notes and are ignored.

paths._note: All paths are relative to the folder that contains this config file.
paths._prepared_note: Phase 0 writes the prepared (reprojected, fixed, clipped) layers here; the other phases read them automatically.

study_area._note: Phase 0 data preparation. source: 'extent' = bounding box of extent_layer (default: all buildings, keeps results identical to a run without Phase 0); 'urban' = the urban polygons (optionally filtered with urban_filter, a QGIS expression such as "MIN_REGION" = 'SWELLENDAM'); 'file' = your own polygon GeoPackage (e.g. digitised in QGIS).
study_area._reference_note: Reference layers (schools, roads, rivers, urban, water...) are clipped to the study area PLUS this buffer, so features just outside it still count (edge effect). Fixed at 1600 m in every release from v1.0.1 on, so Boolean (Phase 2) and MCE (Phase 2b, v2.0) read the SAME prepared data: the largest distance any rule measures is the MCE school factor (1500 m) + 100 m margin. 'auto' = largest distance used by any rule + 100 m. Phase 0 warns if this is smaller than the largest rule distance.
study_area._candidate_note: Candidate layer footprints are SELECTED (Extract by Location), never cut, so their areas stay correct.

layers._note: Each value is BOTH the GeoPackage file stem and the layer name inside it, e.g. dataset/buildings.gpkg|layername=buildings.
layers._optional_note: Shown on the Phase 1 map; used by Phase 2b only when mce.constraints.water_setback or mce.factors.restaurant is enabled (both off by default).

fields._note: Attribute names in the input data. id_candidates is the order used to pick a stable feature ID (for popups and for comparing manual vs. script vs. AI results).

analysis._note: analysis_crs: 'auto' picks the local UTM zone from the buildings extent; or give a code such as 'EPSG:32734' to match the CRS you used in the manual QGIS exercise.

criteria._note: Boolean screening rules (constraints). A building must pass ALL of them.
criteria._river_classes_note: Attribute filter on rivers.waterway before the buffer (e.g. ["river", "stream"]). Empty list = every waterway (the baseline that gives the standard 9 sites). Each run prints the classes found.
criteria._urban_relation_note: 'intersects' keeps buildings touching an urban polygon (original baseline); 'within' requires the whole footprint inside.

population._note: pop_estimate = footprint area / sqm_per_person (the baseline taught in class). pop_estimate_levels also multiplies by building:levels (default_levels when missing).

scoring._note: Ranking of the candidates that passed screening (it never excludes one). Each factor gets a 0-1 score by linear interpolation between 'zero_at_m' (score 0) and 'one_at_m' (score 1). Weights are normalised to sum to 1.

performance._note: Fix geometries always runs. Simplification (Douglas-Peucker) reduces vertices: faster processing, smaller web files. tolerance_m = how far an edge may move.

simplify_analysis._note: Applied to the metric analysis copies BEFORE the spatial steps. Distances to these layers can change by up to tolerance_m. Buildings are NOT listed: simplifying footprints changes their area, which is a selection rule.

simplify_web._note: Applied only to the copies drawn on the web maps (zones, roads, rivers, urban...). Never to the analysis or to the result footprints.

performance._precision_note: Decimal places in GeoJSON output: 6 = about 11 cm, 7 = about 1 cm (larger files).

mce._about: Phase 2b - Multi-Criteria Evaluation (weighted linear combination). The values below are ILLUSTRATIVE teaching defaults: agree on them with your class.

constraints._note: Hard 0/1 rules = 'is it allowed at all?'. Keep only true legal/physical limits here. Set enabled=false to turn one off.
constraints._water_note: OPTIONAL (off by default): keep buildings at least distance_m from any water.gpkg polygon (dams, reservoirs, ponds). Turn on as a class exercise.

factors._note: Standardised 0-1 by linear membership: score 0 at zero_at_m, score 1 at one_at_m. School: closer is better (wider range than the Boolean 1,000 m cut-off, so near-misses are scored, not dropped).
factors._restaurant_note: OPTIONAL (off by default): closer to a restaurant/amenity is better. When enabled it joins the weights below (AHP pairs or direct) as a 4th factor.

weights._note: method 'ahp' derives weights from pairwise comparisons (Saaty 1-9 scale; 'a/b': 3 means a is moderately more important than b). method 'direct' uses the numbers in 'direct'. Pairs/weights for a factor that is switched off are ignored.

selection._note: 'match_boolean' selects as many sites as the Boolean result found (fair comparison); 'top_n' uses top_n; 'min_score' keeps every site with score >= min_score.

sensitivity._note: Each weight is raised and lowered by weight_change (then re-normalised). stability = share of these scenarios in which a selected site stays selected.

web._note: Basemaps: 'osm' and 'esri_imagery' are allowed for teaching with attribution. satellite_max_px limits the local image overlay size so the HTML stays small.
web._credit_note: Shown in the dashboard footer and on the map's attribution line.
